item.title: ‘Two Prosecutors’ Trailer: Ukrainian Auteur Sergei Loznitsa Returns with a Harrowing Soviet Union Legal Thriller
item.description: Exclusive: The 2025 Cannes favorite opens in New York on March 20 and Los Angeles on March 27.

item.title: In Berlin-Bound ‘Tristan Forever,’ a Doctor, a Penguin, and 230 People Converge on a Volcanic Island — First Look
item.description: Exclusive: The Berlin-set docufiction follows a Parisian doctor to a volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean, where he hopes to find permanent residence.

item.title: ‘The Singers’ Trailer: An Oscar Short Nominee for Our Times, from a Story Written in 1850
item.description: Exclusive: Directed by Sam Davis, Netflix's Live Action Short Oscar nominee adapts Ivan Turgenev's 19th-century Russian story to a dive bar where the regulars find catharsis through impromptu singing.

item.title: ‘Omaha’ Trailer: A Heartbreaking John Magaro Anchors This Festival Favorite
item.description: Cole Webley's deep-feeling feature was a hit on the festival circuit and is now (finally!) bound for a much-deserved theatrical release.

item.title: ‘Honey Bunch’ Review: Strong Performances Leaven a Derivative Retro-Thriller
item.description: Dusty Mancinelli and Madeleine Sims-Fewer’s Gothic horror often loses sight of its core romance in favor of its many references.

item.title: James Van Der Beek, ‘Dawson’s Creek’ Star and Generational TV Icon, Dead at 48
item.description: Van Der Beek, who had been battling cancer since 2023, recently starred on TV's "Overcompensating" and was excellent in generational coming-of-age movies like "Varsity Blues" and "The Rules of Attraction."

item.title: How Oscar Contender Will Tracy Pulled Off That Crazy ‘Bugonia’ Script
item.description: The Emmy-winning "Succession" writer explains the title: "It sounded a little bit like a mental disorder you might come down with."

item.title: First ‘Conclave,’ Now ‘Hamnet’ — Focus Features Has Found the Secret to International Box Office Hits for Grownups
item.description: Chloé Zhao's Oscar-nominated drama has quietly made $70 million worldwide in a slow burn rollout rarely seen today.

item.title: Bud Cort, ‘Harold and Maude’ Star, Dead at 77
item.description: The character actor also starred in films like "Brewster McCloud" and "The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou."

item.description: Applications for IndieWire and The American Pavilion's Cannes Intensive are open through February 25.
